display.purpose: One per page: the home widget's headline and the pricing headline. The accented word sits in an em that turns hot orange.

headline.purpose: Section headings on the sky; legal and create titles at clamp(36px, 5vw, 56px).

title.purpose: Legal sub-headings and plan names at 24px; 20px in the launcher bar. Smaller widget titles switch to Onest 700.

price.purpose: The plan price, with its period in Onest 600 15px.

wordmark.purpose: TypePlay in the status bar (24px) and footer (18px); 'Play' in Sun Amber.

lead.purpose: The sentence under a section headline, On Sky Muted, max 60ch.

body.purpose: Descriptions, quoted prompts, bubbles and FAQ answers inside widgets; 17px in the ship and CTA widgets and the textarea.

read.purpose: Legal sheet paragraphs and lists in #2b2147, max 68ch.

label.purpose: Widget labels, notice title, dock caption, slot names, the pill; app names at 14px; nav links at 500.

button.purpose: Every .button; also listing names and FAQ questions at 700/17px.

figures.purpose: Measured facts only: tier, minutes, versions, dates, availability. Tabular numerals, usually muted.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing, in CSS (--ease-out) and in Motion (AppIcon, Launcher, Notice).

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Declared as --ease-in-out; unused in the build.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Colour and transform transitions on buttons, pills, links, icons, notice, listings.

motion.name: press-icon
motion.purpose: Active state of an app icon's picture.

motion.name: press-sheet
motion.purpose: Active state of the notice and listings.

motion.name: app-open
motion.purpose: The icon zooms into the launcher frame; a fade under reduced motion (layoutId disabled).

motion.name: launcher-fade
motion.purpose: The launcher overlay's opacity, always on.

motion.name: notice-in
motion.purpose: The notification's single entrance on load; skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: build-loop
motion.value: 6s ease-out infinite, 4 layers staggered 0.9s, from translateY(12%)
motion.purpose: The 'Your game' icon assembling; the label swaps on the same 6s clock (58-62% and 80-84%). Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.value: 3px solid var(--sun), offset 3px (2px on the prompt field)
motion.purpose: Every :focus-visible; the global rule also sets border-radius 6px on elements without their own radius.

breakpoints.name: home-4-col
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: 4-column home grid, 96px icons.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: dock, chat, plans and ship widgets stack.

breakpoints.name: launcher-stack
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: the launcher info row stacks.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: names-only icons, nav keeps Pricing and Sign in, prompt field stacks, 32px widget radius.

breakpoints.name: short-desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Tighter hero so the dock stays inside the first screen.

narrative.overview:
The public site is a phone home screen. Every page sits on one continuous dusk-desert wallpaper drawn flat, in bands of colour, exactly as the product's agent draws its 2D games, and the visitor's sentence becomes an app icon on that screen. Content lives in opaque white widgets and an ink dock laid over the sky, the way widgets sit on a wallpaper; the ground (sun and dunes) rises at the bottom of the home hero and again at the end of every page, under the footer. Hot orange is the one thing to press.

It refuses the category's dark centred hero with a glowing prompt box and a row of equal cards. The density is that of a tablet home screen: an 8-column icon grid at desktop width, four columns on tablets, names-only icons on phones. Nothing floats: there are no shadows, blurs, gradients or glass; depth is one flat surface over another. Copy is plain player language, and the only proof is real games, their real prompts and measured minutes.
keyCharacteristics: One fixed wallpaper (five sky bands) under every page; the ground belongs to a section, never to the wallpaper, so reading text never crosses the sand.
Two surfaces only: opaque paper widgets and ink bars (dock, footer, launcher).
Hot orange (#ff5a36) is the single action colour, and text on it is always ink (#170d33).
One corner-radius system: icons 25%, widgets 40px, dock 34px, fields 20px, buttons 15px.
Gabarito 900 display, Onest for everything read or tapped, Martian Mono for measured figures; Phosphor icons.

One motion grammar: the app-open zoom from icon to full game frame, the notification's single entrance, the "Your game" icon assembling on a 6-second clock; press feedback by scale; a reduced-motion fallback for each.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Hot Rule
rules.body: Text on hot orange is always ink: white on #ff5a36 is 3.1:1, ink is 5.9:1. The lead plan's button therefore inverts to ink with white text rather than putting orange on orange.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Hot orange marks what to press, plus the one accented word of a display headline. It is never a band, a border or a background for reading text.

rules.name: The Sun Rule
rules.body: Sun amber is for focus rings, the wordmark and the drawn sun; it never fills a button.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Gabarito only for headlines, titles, prices and the wordmark; Onest for everything read or tapped; Martian Mono only for measured figures. No fourth face, no italics.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a headline: no kicker, no small-caps label, no section number.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: The sky is fixed and shared by every page; the ground is owned by a section. Never put the dunes in the wallpaper, and never let reading text scroll over the sand.

rules.name: The Overlap Rule
rules.body: Depth is one flat surface over another. No shadow, blur, glass or gradient, including on hover.

rules.name: The Two Surfaces Rule
rules.body: Everything sits on paper or on ink. Recessed areas are Field on paper and Ink Recess on ink; there is no third surface tone.

rules.name: The Five Radii Rule
rules.body: A new surface takes one of the five tokens: icon, widget, dock, field or button. A pill is the only exception.

dos: Do put every page on the fixed wallpaper and end it with the ground band and the ink footer; the home hero is the only other place the ground appears and the only place with a sun.
Do put content in opaque paper widgets (40px) or ink bars (34px), and recess inside them with Field or Ink Recess.
Do use hot orange for the one thing to press and set its text in ink (#170d33).
Do use the five radii: icon 25%, widget 40px, dock 34px, field 20px, button 15px.
Do set figures (tier, minutes, versions, dates) in Martian Mono 11px with tabular numerals, muted.
Do gate hover behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and give touch a press scale instead.
Do give every authored motion a reduced-motion fallback: a fade for the zoom, no entrance for the notice, a static assembled icon.
Do write plain player language (game, build, edit, version, credits, Fast / Smart / Best, export) and prove with real games, real prompts and measured minutes.
donts: Don't add shadows, blur, glass, gradients or borders; depth is overlap only.
Don't put white text on hot orange (3.1:1); the lead plan's button inverts to ink for this reason.
Don't let text scroll over the sand: the ground belongs to a section, never to the wallpaper.
Don't put an eyebrow, kicker or label above a headline, and don't use em-dashes anywhere in copy.
Don't copy a phone's status bar literally: no time, battery or "9:41".
Don't add a fourth typeface or italics, and don't set Gabarito below 20px except the footer wordmark (18px); smaller titles are Onest 700.
Don't add hover effects beyond a colour change; the three authored moments are the whole motion budget.
Don't use stock illustration or photography; pictures are flat SVG drawn in code (wallpaper, ground, assembling icon) or real game screenshots.
Don't let the drawn SVGs (wallpaper, ground, building icon) drift from the colour tokens: they use literal hex, so a token change is also an SVG change.
